title: Coast Guard command centers during Hurricane Harvey
description: During Hurricane Harvey call centers took over 26,000 calls. Chief Petty Officer Charles Froberg, an operations specialist at the 8th Coast Guard District command center, discusses what his experience was like trying to coordinate multiple rescues during one Houston's largest natural disasters.
keywords: Harvey, Operations Specialist, command center, Hurricane Harvey, Coast Guard

transcript.text: - [Lt. Allen] This is State Command Center,
Lieutenant Allen speaking.
- [Lady On The Phone] Oh, I could cry,
okay, finally got through,
okay, there's a family stuck on the roof, are you ready...
(intense music)
- It was very stressful, I ate, drank, and slept Harvey
for 24 hours a day the entire time it was going on.
At the beginning we was doing it as normal,
writing it down on paper.
As it began to increase in volume the way it did,
we started entering into
the Homeland Security Information Network,
and the GeoSuite applications,
which allowed us to rapidly disseminate it
to multiple agencies, State EOCs,
and Search and Rescue units, to respond.
Social media was a big part of it,
we were getting the same report multiple times,
so we would take it, regardless if we heard it or not,
and enter it, and allow the next level of responders
to kind of weed through those reports.
It was such a long lasting storm,
stalled out over Houston.
Seemed like it was never gonna stop.
So we just adapted and overcame and got the job done.
